summary_paragraph: A female patient with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, antiphospholipid syndrome, pulmonary hypertension, and chronic vertigo was admitted after missing two dialysis sessions due to severe vertigo and vomiting. She presented with hyperkalemia (potassium 6.7) at an outside hospital, received emergency treatment, and was transferred for further management. She underwent two consecutive hemodialysis sessions, which normalized her potassium and improved her symptoms. Meclizine was continued for vertigo, and physical therapy recommended outpatient vestibular rehabilitation. The patient refused telemetry due to adhesive allergy but was closely monitored. She remained stable, was discharged home in good condition, and advised to monitor weight, attend dialysis regularly, and follow up with her primary care provider.
